Rep. Jason Crow criticizes presidential priorities and U.S. policy in August social media posts
Rep. Jason Crow, a U.S. Congressman representing Colorado’s 6th district since 2019, posted a series of critical statements on August 19, 2026, addressing the President's priorities, the ongoing conflict with Iran, and the nation’s rising debt.
In one post from August 19 at 16:31 UTC, Crow wrote: "Our President is focused on his taxpayer-funded golden ballroom. He says he's 'very good at flagpoles.' The American people wish he'd lower costs & end his Middle East wars."
Later that day at 19:42 UTC, he commented on foreign policy developments by stating, "The war with Iran is a complete disaster. Maybe Hegseth should focus on his current job before auditioning for the next one."
Addressing fiscal issues in an evening post at 21:48 UTC, Crow recalled past promises and criticized recent legislative actions: "In 2016, Trump said he’d get rid of the national debt 'fairly quickly.' A decade later, America’s debt just hit $40 TRILLION. The Republican One Big Ugly Bill adds over $4 trillion alone—all to shamefully give tax breaks to billionaires and corporations."
Crow has served as the representative for Colorado's 6th District since replacing Mike Coffman in 2019. Born in Madison, Wisconsin in 1979 and currently residing in Aurora, Crow holds degrees from the University of Wisconsin–Madison (BA) and the University of Denver (JD).
